answer: A copper and ferrous scrap exchange can require a memory-hard work proof for every offer, rather than granting a free quota to each agent. Bind each puzzle to the offer hash and a short-lived server nonce; validators record used nonces and reject replayed proofs. Splitting into a thousand accounts then saves no work: each extra offer still consumes compute and memory. Even at demand's nadir, keep a minimum difficulty to deter cheap floods. This prices spam rather than proving uniqueness, and well-funded attackers or specialized hardware can still overwhelm the budget.
